hindi: जिह्वा-निर्लेखन तीक्ष्ण न हों और टेढ़े हों; और जो मल जिह्वा के मूल में स्थित है और उच्छ्वास को रोकता है,
english: Tongue-scrapers should be not sharp and curved; and the waste (mala) which lies at the root of the tongue and obstructs breathing,
notes: The relative clause 'yat ... malam' is completed by 'tena' in 76a; the sentence runs on into 76. anṛju 'not straight' = curved (bent so as to scrape).

hindi: उससे दुर्गन्ध प्राप्त होती है; इसलिए जिह्वा को खुरचना चाहिए। वैशद्य, रुचि और सौगन्ध्य चाहने वाले को मुख से ये धारण करने चाहिए:
english: by that one acquires foul smell; therefore one should scrape the tongue. One who desires clearness (vaiśadya), relish and fragrance should hold with the mouth the following:
notes: 'tena' picks up the relative clause of 75b. 76b introduces the list of mouth-fresheners in 77; the sentence continues into 77 (not a grouping error). Subject of 'bhajate' is unexpressed (one / the person).

hindi: जाती, कटुक और पूग के तथा लवङ्ग के फल; कक्कोल का फल, तथा ताम्बूल का शुभ पत्र; तथा कर्पूर-निर्यास और सूक्ष्म एला के फल।
english: the fruits of jātī, kaṭuka and pūga, and of lavaṅga; the fruit of kakkola, and likewise the fine leaf of tāmbūla; likewise the exudate of karpūra, and the fruits of the small elā.
notes: Identifications (notes only): jātī(phala) = nutmeg, Myristica fragrans (standard); pūga = areca nut, Areca catechu (standard); lavaṅga = clove, Syzygium aromaticum (standard; the 'fruits' are the dried buds); kakkola = cubeb, Piper cubeba (probable; disputed); tāmbūla = betel leaf, Piper betle (standard); karpūra = camphor, from Cinnamomum camphora (standard); sūkṣmailā = small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum (standard). kaṭuka: disputed; it may be a separate item, or 'jātī-kaṭuka' may be read together as one item (the pungent jātī fruit, i.e. nutmeg); taken here as a three-member dvandva. Three printed lines in one numbered verse, as in the edition.
lines_deva: कक्कोलस्य फलं पत्रं ताम्बूलस्य शुभं तथा
lines_iast: kakkolasya phalaṃ patraṃ tāmbūlasya śubhaṃ tathā

hindi: हनुओं का बल, स्वर का बल, मुख का उत्तम उपचय, और उत्तम रस-ज्ञान, और अन्न में श्रेष्ठ रुचि होती है।
english: There would be strength of the jaws, strength of voice, excellent fullness of the face, excellent perception of taste (rasa), and the best relish for food.
notes: These results (78–80) belong to holding oil in the mouth (taila-gaṇḍūṣa-dhāraṇa), named only in 80b; 78–80 are one statement. Optative 'syāt' rendered 'there would be'.
lines_deva: स्यात् परं च रसज्ञानमन्ने च रुचिरुत्तमा
lines_iast: syāt paraṃ ca rasajñānamanne ca ruciruttamā

hindi: और उसे कण्ठ-शोष नहीं होता, न ओठों के फटने का भय रहता है; और दाँत क्षय को प्राप्त नहीं होते और दृढ़-मूल होते हैं।
english: And he would have no dryness of the throat, nor fear of cracking of the lips; and the teeth do not decay, and they become firm-rooted.
notes: Continues the results of oil-holding (see 80b).
lines_deva: न च दन्ताः क्षयं यान्ति दृढमूला भवन्ति च
lines_iast: na ca dantāḥ kṣayaṃ yānti dṛḍhamūlā bhavanti ca

words.gloss: from holding a mouthful of oil

hindi: तैल-गण्डूष-धारण से दाँतों में शूल नहीं होता, न अम्ल से उनमें सिहरन होती है, और वे अत्यन्त कठोर भक्ष्यों को भी चबा लेते हैं।
english: From holding a mouthful of oil (taila-gaṇḍūṣa), the teeth do not ache, nor are they set on edge by sour things, and they chew even very hard foods.
notes: Subject 'teeth' is carried over from 79b. hṛṣyante: 'dantaharṣa', the teeth being set on edge (hypersensitivity); Hindi renders it as सिहरन (tingling). 'parān' taken adverbially-adjectivally as 'extremely (hard)'; alternatively 'other (hard) foods'.
lines_deva: न शूल्यन्ते न चाम्लेन हृष्यन्ते भक्षयन्ति च
lines_iast: na śūlyante na cāmlena hṛṣyante bhakṣayanti ca

words.gloss: whose head is moist with sneha

hindi: जिसका सिर नित्य स्नेह से आर्द्र रहता है उसे शिरःशूल नहीं होता; न खालित्य, न पालित्य, और न केश झड़ते हैं।
english: For one whose head is always moist with oil (sneha), headache does not arise; there is no baldness, no greying, nor do the hairs fall out.
notes: khālitya and pālitya are the Āyurvedic names for baldness/alopecia and premature greying (standard).
lines_deva: न खालित्यं न पालित्यं न केशाः प्रपतन्ति च
lines_iast: na khālityaṃ na pālityaṃ na keśāḥ prapatanti ca

hindi: शिर के कपालों का बल विशेष रूप से बढ़ता है; और केश दृढ़-मूल, लम्बे और काले होते हैं।
english: The strength of the skull-bones increases especially, and the hairs become firm-rooted, long and black.
lines_deva: दृढमूलाश्च दीर्घाश्च कृष्णाः केशा भवन्ति च
lines_iast: dṛḍhamūlāśca dīrghāśca kṛṣṇāḥ keśā bhavanti ca

hindi: सिर पर तैल-निषेवण से इन्द्रियाँ प्रसन्न होती हैं, मुख अच्छी त्वचा वाला होता है, और निद्रा-लाभ तथा सुख होता है।
english: From the use of oil on the head the senses become clear, the face has good skin, and there would be getting of sleep and happiness.
notes: 'sukham' may be a second subject ('and happiness') or adverbial ('getting sleep easily'); the first is followed in the translation. 'mūrdhni' (loc.) goes with 'taila-niṣevaṇāt': use of oil on the head.

hindi: नित्य कर्ण-तर्पण से वात से उत्पन्न कर्ण-रोग नहीं होते, न मन्या और हनु का संग्रह होता है, न ऊँचा सुनना, न बाधिर्य होता है।
english: From daily karṇatarpaṇa (filling the ears with oil) there are no ear diseases arising from Vāta, no stiffness of the neck (manyā) and jaw, no hearing only of loud sounds, and no deafness.

text_flags.why: the word for deafness is bādhirya (from badhira); v for b is a common confusion

notes: 'uccaiḥ śrutiḥ' = hearing only when spoken loudly, i.e. hardness of hearing. manyā = the side/back muscles of the neck; manyā-hanu-saṃgraha is stiffness of neck and jaw (torticollis / lockjaw-like states; probable). karṇatarpaṇa = ear-oiling ('satiating the ears').

hindi: जैसे स्नेह-अभ्यङ्ग से घड़ा, स्नेह-विमर्दन से चर्म, और उपाङ्ग से अक्ष दृढ़ और क्लेश सहने योग्य हो जाता है,
english: Just as a pot from being smeared with oil, leather from being rubbed with oil, and an axle from lubrication become firm and able to bear strain,
notes: The simile is completed by 'tathā' in 86a; 85–86 are one sentence. upāṅga = greasing (of an axle).

hindi: वैसे ही अभ्यङ्ग से शरीर दृढ़ और अच्छी त्वचा वाला हो जाता है, उसकी मारुत-जनित बाधा शान्त हो जाती है, और वह क्लेश तथा व्यायाम को सहने योग्य होता है।
english: so from massage (abhyaṅga) the body becomes firm and of good skin, with its troubles from Vāta (māruta) calmed, and able to endure strain and exercise.

hindi: स्पर्शन में वायु अधिक होता है, और स्पर्शन त्वचा पर आश्रित है; और अभ्यङ्ग त्वचा के लिए परम हितकर है; इसलिए मनुष्य को उसका नियमित सेवन करना चाहिए।
english: Vāta (vāyu) predominates in the sense of touch (sparśana), and the sense of touch resides in the skin; and massage is supremely beneficial to the skin; therefore a man should practise it regularly.
notes: 'param' may also be read as an adjective with abhyaṅgaḥ ('the best thing for the skin'); sense is the same.

hindi: और अभ्यङ्ग-सेवी का शरीर अभिघात से आहत होने पर, अथवा कभी बल-कर्म में, अत्यधिक विकार को प्राप्त नहीं होता।
english: And the body of one who practises massage, when struck by an injury, or at any time in strenuous work, does not undergo excessive disorder.

words.gloss: with limbs smooth to touch and well-built

hindi: नित्य अभ्यङ्ग से मनुष्य सुस्पर्श और उपचित अङ्गों वाला, बलवान्, प्रियदर्शन और अल्प-जरा वाला भी होता है।
english: From regular massage a man becomes one whose limbs are smooth to the touch and well-built, strong, pleasing to look at, and also of little ageing.

text_flags.why: metre: 'bhavatyaṅganityatvān' has 7 syllables where 8 are needed; 'abhyaṅga' (the topic of 85–89) restores both metre and sense; the printed 'aṅga' looks like a lost 'bhya'

notes: Split follows the suggested reading abhyaṅga-nityatvāt; the printed token gives aṅga-nityatvāt 'from constancy of the limbs', which makes poor sense.

hindi: पाद-अभ्यङ्ग के निषेवण से पैरों का खरत्व, स्तब्धता, रूक्षता, श्रम और सुप्ति तत्काल शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: Roughness, stiffness, dryness, fatigue and numbness of the feet subside immediately from the practice of foot-massage.

text_flags.why: 'viṣevaṇa' is not a word; 'niṣevaṇa' (use, practice) is the form used elsewhere in this chapter (83b, 96b); typing error v for n

notes: 'sadya eva' rendered 'immediately'. supti = numbness (loss of sensation).
lines_deva: खरत्वं स्तब्धता रौक्ष्यं श्रमः सुप्तिश्च पादयोः
lines_iast: kharatvaṃ stabdhatā raukṣyaṃ śramaḥ suptiśca pādayoḥ

hindi: और पैरों में सौकुमार्य, बल और स्थिरता उत्पन्न होती है; दृष्टि प्रसाद को प्राप्त होती है और मारुत शान्त होता है।
english: And softness, strength and steadiness of the feet arise; the sight gains clarity, and Vāta (māruta) is calmed.
lines_deva: जायते सौकुमार्यं च बलं स्थैर्यं च पादयोः
lines_iast: jāyate saukumāryaṃ ca balaṃ sthairyaṃ ca pādayoḥ

hindi: पाद-अभ्यङ्ग से न गृध्रसी-वात होता है, न पैरों का स्फुटन, और न पैरों में सिरा और स्नायु का संकोच होता है।
english: By foot-massage there would be no gṛdhrasī-vāta, no cracking of the feet, and no contraction of the vessels (sirā) and sinews (snāyu) in the feet.
notes: gṛdhrasī = sciatica (standard). The second 'pādayoḥ' is read as locative ('in the feet'); the first as genitive.
lines_deva: न च स्याद्गृध्रसीवातः पादयोः स्फुटनं न च
lines_iast: na ca syādgṛdhrasīvātaḥ pādayoḥ sphuṭanaṃ na ca

hindi: शरीर-परिमार्जन दुर्गन्ध, गौरव, तन्द्रा, कण्डू, मल, अरोचक और स्वेद की बीभत्सता को नष्ट करता है।
english: Rubbing the body (parimārjana) removes foul smell, heaviness, drowsiness, itching, dirt (mala), loss of relish (arocaka) and the loathsomeness of sweat.
notes: parimārjana is usually understood as rubbing/cleansing the body (by commentators as udvartana, rubbing with powders); the text says only 'rubbing'. arocaka = anorexia (standard).

hindi: स्नान पवित्र, वृष्य, आयुष्य, श्रम-स्वेद-मल को दूर करने वाला, शरीर के बल का संधान करने वाला और परम ओजस्कर है।
english: Bathing is purifying, aphrodisiac (vṛṣya), promotes life, removes fatigue, sweat and dirt, restores bodily strength, and is supremely productive of ojas (vital essence).
notes: sandhāna literally 'joining, uniting'; here 'restoring/sustaining' bodily strength.

hindi: निर्मल वस्त्र का धारण काम्य, यशस्य, आयुष्य, अलक्ष्मी-नाशक, प्रहर्षक, श्रीमत्, पारिषद और प्रशस्त है।
english: Wearing clean clothes is pleasing, brings fame, promotes life, destroys misfortune (alakṣmī), gladdens, is graceful, fit for assemblies, and commended.

hindi: गन्ध और माल्य का निषेवण वृष्य, सौगन्ध्य, आयुष्य, काम्य, पुष्टि और बल देने वाला, सौमनस्य और अलक्ष्मी-नाशक है।
english: The use of perfumes and garlands is aphrodisiac, yields fragrance, promotes life, is pleasing, gives nourishment and strength, yields cheerfulness, and destroys misfortune (alakṣmī).

text_flags.why: metre (9 syllables in the first half of the line) and the parallels in 94–99 give āyuṣyam; 'āyuṣayaṃ' is a typing error
'-ghna' (destroying) as in 95a; 'ghra' is a typing error

notes: saugandhya and saumanasya are abstract nouns used as predicates ('is fragrance', 'is cheerfulness', i.e. brings them); kept literal in translation.

hindi: रत्न और आभरण का धारण धन्य, मङ्गल्य, आयुष्य, श्रीमत्, व्यसन-नाशक, हर्षक, काम्य और ओजस्य है।
english: Wearing gems and ornaments brings fortune, is auspicious, promotes life, is graceful, removes calamity (vyasana), gladdens, is pleasing, and promotes ojas.
notes: ratnābharaṇa may also be 'ornaments of gems' (tat-puruṣa) rather than 'gems and ornaments' (dvandva).

hindi: पैरों और मल-मार्गों का बार-बार शौच करना मेध्य, पवित्र, आयुष्य और अलक्ष्मी तथा कलि का नाशक है।
english: Frequent cleansing of the feet and the excretory passages (mala-mārga) promotes intellect (medhya), is purifying, promotes life, and destroys misfortune (alakṣmī) and strife (kali).
notes: kali = strife, discord (or ill luck).

hindi: केश, श्मश्रु, नख आदि का कल्पन और संप्रसाधन पौष्टिक, वृष्य, आयुष्य, शुचि और रूप को निखारने वाला है।
english: Trimming and dressing of hair, beard, nails and the like is nourishing, aphrodisiac, promotes life, is clean, and brightens the appearance.

hindi: पादत्र का धारण चक्षुष्य, स्पर्शन के लिए हितकर, पैरों के व्यसन को दूर करने वाला, बल्य, पराक्रम को सुखद बनाने वाला और वृष्य है।
english: Wearing footwear (pādatra) is good for the eyes, beneficial to the sense of touch (sparśana), removes injury (vyasana) to the feet, is strengthening, makes exertion easy, and is aphrodisiac.

text_flags.why: metathesis: 'spraśana' for 'sparśana' (touch), the word used in 87a

notes: parākrama here probably 'exertion, moving about (walking)'.

words.gloss: keeping off heat, wind, dust and rain

hindi: छत्र-धारण ईति का प्रशमन करने वाला, बल्य, गुप्ति, आवरण और कल्याण करने वाला, तथा घाम, वायु, रज और जल को रोकने वाला कहा जाता है।
english: Carrying an umbrella is said to ward off calamity (īti), to be strengthening, to give protection, cover and welfare, and to keep off heat, wind, dust and rain.
notes: īti = calamity (in the classical lists, plagues such as excessive rain, drought, locusts). 'śaṅkara' = conferring welfare; it may also be read 'guptyāvaraṇa-śaṅkaram' = giving the welfare of protective cover. 'rajombu' = rajaḥ + ambu; no avagraha inside the compound, as usual in print.

hindi: दण्ड-धारण लड़खड़ाने वाले को सहारा देने वाला, और शत्रुओं का नाशक, अवलम्बन, आयुष्य और भय को दूर करने वाला है।
english: Carrying a staff is a support for one who stumbles, a destroyer of enemies, a prop, promotes life, and removes fear.

hindi: जैसे नगर का स्वामी नगर के प्रति और रथी रथ के प्रति, वैसे ही बुद्धिमान् को अपने शरीर के कृत्यों में सावधान रहना चाहिए।
english: As a city-lord for his city, and as a chariot-owner for his chariot, so the wise man should be attentive in the duties of his own body.
notes: nagarin = owner/lord of a city; rathin = owner or rider of a chariot (also 'chariot-warrior'). 'kṛtyeṣu avahitaḥ' is understood with each comparison.

hindi: और यहाँ यह है — जीविका के जो उपाय धर्म के अविरोधी हों उनका सेवन करना चाहिए, और शम तथा अध्ययन का भी; इस प्रकार वह सुख प्राप्त करता है।
english: And here there is: one should resort to those means of livelihood which are not opposed to dharma, and also to tranquillity and study; thus one attains happiness.
notes: 'bhavati cātra' is the lead-in formula introducing a verse, printed inside line a; it is outside the metre. 'śamam adhyayanaṃ ca' are further objects of 'niṣeveta'.

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक — मात्रा, द्रव्य, मात्रा पर आश्रित गुरुता और लघुता; जिन द्रव्यों का अभ्यास निन्दित है, और जिनका प्रशस्त है;
english: Here, the verses: measure (mātrā); substances; heaviness and lightness depending on measure; the substances whose habitual use is censured, and those whose is praised;

text_flags.why: possible: the half-line after the lead-in has 15 syllables, one short of 16; a 'ca' after 'mātrāṃ' would complete the metre. Not applied

notes: 'tatra ślokāḥ' introduces the chapter's summary verses (105–111), one running list of the topics; its predicate 'guṇāḥ ... uktāḥ' comes in 111. The lead-in is outside the metre.
lines_deva: तत्र श्लोकाः --- मात्रा द्रव्याणि मात्रां संश्रित्य गुरुलाघवम्
द्रव्याणां गर्हितोऽभ्यासो येषां, येषां च शस्यते
lines_iast: tatra ślokāḥ --- mātrā dravyāṇi mātrāṃ saṃśritya gurulāghavam
dravyāṇāṃ garhito'bhyāso yeṣāṃ, yeṣāṃ ca śasyate

hindi: अञ्जन; धूमवर्ति; वर्ति की त्रिविध कल्पना; धूमपान के गुण, उसके काल, और पान का मान, और किसके लिए कौन-सा;
english: collyrium (añjana); the smoking-stick (dhūmavarti); the threefold preparation of sticks; the benefits of smoking; its times; and the measure of smoking, and for whom which;
notes: Part of the summary list. 'yasya yat' = which (kind or measure) for whom. 'pāna' here = drinking (inhaling) smoke.
lines_deva: धूमपानगुणाः कालाः पानमानं च यस्य यत्
lines_iast: dhūmapānaguṇāḥ kālāḥ pānamānaṃ ca yasya yat

hindi: व्यापत्ति के चिह्न, भैषज्य; जिनके लिए धूम निषिद्ध है; वह कैसे पीना चाहिए; नेत्र किससे बना हो, और जिसके लिए किस प्रकार का हो;
english: the signs of complications (vyāpatti) and the remedy; for whom smoke is forbidden; how it is to be drunk; of what the tube (netra) is made, and for whom of what kind;
notes: Part of the summary list. netra = the smoking-pipe. 'bhaiṣajyam' = the remedy (for those complications).
lines_deva: पेयो यथा यन्मयं च नेत्रं यस्य च यद्विधम्
lines_iast: peyo yathā yanmayaṃ ca netraṃ yasya ca yadvidham

words.gloss: to be done through the nose

hindi: नस्य-कर्म के गुण; नासिका से जो कार्य है, वह कैसे और कब; दन्तपवन को कैसे चबाना चाहिए, कौन सा, किन गुणों वाला, और क्या;
english: the benefits of nasal therapy (nasya); what is to be done through the nose, how and when; how one should chew the tooth-stick (dantapavana), which one, of what qualities, and what;

text_flags.why: possible: 'yad yadguṇaṃ' (which, of what quality) makes sense; 'yaṅguṇa' is not a word and looks like ṅg typed for dg

notes: Part of the summary list. The final 'ca yat' repeats the relative and adds little; the series of relatives (yat, yathā, yadā) stands for the topics of the chapter.

hindi: किस प्रयोजन से और कौन सी वस्तुएँ कवल-ग्रह में मुख से धारण करनी चाहिए; तैल के जो गुण बताए गए, और शिरस्-तैल के जो गुण हैं;
english: for what purpose and which things are to be held with the mouth in gargling (kavala-graha); the benefits of oil that were indicated, and those which are the benefits of head-oil;
notes: Part of the summary list. 'kavalagrahe' (loc.) is taken with 'dhāryāṇi' (to be held in gargling). kavala = a mouthful moved about in the mouth, as against gaṇḍūṣa (held).
lines_deva: तैलस्य ये गुणा दिष्टाः शिरस्तैलगुणाश्च ये
lines_iast: tailasya ye guṇā diṣṭāḥ śirastailaguṇāśca ye

hindi: कर्ण-तैल में, तथा अभ्यङ्ग में, पाद-अभ्यङ्ग में, अङ्ग-मार्जन में; स्नान में, और शुद्ध वस्त्र में, सौगन्ध्य में, रत्न-धारण में;
english: in ear-oil, likewise in massage, in foot-massage, in rubbing the body; in bathing, and in clean clothing, in fragrance, in wearing gems;
notes: The locatives of 110–111 depend on 'guṇāḥ ... uktāḥ' in 111 (the benefits stated in these matters).
lines_deva: स्नाने वाससि शुद्धे च सौगन्ध्ये रत्नधारणे
lines_iast: snāne vāsasi śuddhe ca saugandhye ratnadhāraṇe

hindi: शौच में, लोमों के संहरण में, पादत्र और छत्र के धारण में, तथा दण्ड-धारण में — इस मात्राशितीय में गुण कहे गए हैं।
english: in cleansing, in removing hair, in wearing footwear and umbrella, and likewise in carrying a staff: the benefits have been stated in this Mātrāśitīya.
notes: End of the summary list (105–111). Mātrāśitīya is the chapter's name ('on the measure of eating'); the word 'chapter' is not in the text. 'tathā' is placed with 'daṇḍadhāraṇe' in the translation; it may also simply mean 'thus (stated)'.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में मात्राशितीय नामक पाँचवाँ अध्याय, पूर्ण।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Ślokasthāna (section), the fifth chapter named Mātrāśitīya, completed.
notes: Colophon. 'samāptaḥ' is printed and is rendered as the participle 'completed' (Hindi पूर्ण), keeping the colophon verbless. Ślokasthāna is the name this edition uses for the first section (also called Sūtrasthāna).
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने मात्राशितीयो नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne mātrāśitīyo nāma pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
